intro: Logan voters elected me in 2023. My colleagues chose me as Vice Chair in 2025 and Chair in 2026. Council decisions are made together, and every item below links to the official minutes so you can check the record yourself.

items.title: Made room for eight starter homes families could actually buy
items.summary: I seconded the 2024 street right-of-way change at 100 West and 600 South that created the land for River Crossing, a city partnership with Visionary Homes. The eight income-qualified townhomes sold for about $279,000, about $40,000 below appraisal, and all sold within about a month. A five-year owner-occupancy rule keeps them from being flipped.

items.title: Made it easier for homeowners to add an accessory apartment
items.summary: During the 2024 rewrite of Logan's accessory dwelling unit (ADU) and short-term rental rules, I pointed out that the 6,000-square-foot minimum lot for an ADU was redundant. The council removed it. I also proposed letting owner-occupied short-term rentals operate under neighbor-friendly limits. The ordinance passed 5–0.

items.title: Adopted the Logan 2045 General Plan
items.summary: This is Logan's first full general plan since 2007, adopted after a 17-month process with neighborhood meetings across the city. As Chair, I pushed to keep design requirements from driving up the cost of new homes. The plan now guides where housing, jobs, parks and roads go for the next 20 years.

items.title: Funded a west-side fire station without raising the typical homeowner's total tax bill
items.summary: Cache County cut its fire levy because Logan residents were paying for county fire service they didn't receive. As Chair, I led a months-long review of alternatives. The council then shifted that same amount, about $59 on a median home, to build Fire Station 73 and keep a police officer on the street. The county line on your bill went down and the city line went up by about the same amount. The council approved it 5–0.

items.title: Cast the only vote against the 2024 property tax rate increase
items.summary: I said the city didn't yet have the data to justify raising the rate. I suggested using reserves to cover a position mid-year if it was needed.

items.title: Kept Logan out of a risky 20-year power contract
items.summary: I moved to approve a smaller natural-gas 'peaker' plant for peak demand. I opposed signing Logan onto a large baseload plant because of the financial risk of a 20-year commitment. In January 2025 the council voted 4–1 not to join.

items.title: Served on the city's Audit Committee
items.summary: I reviewed the city's quarterly finances and helped select a new independent auditor in 2025.

items.title: Opened City Hall with monthly office hours
items.summary: The Mayor and council members now hold open office hours on the first Tuesday of every month at 4:30 p.m. at City Hall. No appointment is needed.

items.title: Put the data center question in front of the public first
items.summary: When data center proposals started coming to Cache Valley, I scheduled a special meeting as Chair. The council passed a 180-day pause 5–0 so the city could write rules before any project arrived. I then scheduled two public open houses so residents could ask questions and shape those rules.

items.title: Made council reports a standing part of every meeting
items.summary: As Chair, I added a standing agenda item to every meeting where council members report publicly on their boards, neighborhood meetings and anything residents should know about.

items.title: Pushed for more public hearings
items.summary: I asked for a second public hearing before the council finalized the 2024 ADU and short-term rental rules. In 2025, I voted against moving changes to the wetland setback rules forward without another public hearing.

items.title: Made walking and biking part of Logan's transportation plan
items.summary: As council liaison to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee, I pushed for the city's transportation master plan to build in safe walking and biking routes. I joined UDOT's walk audit of Highway 89/91 and promoted Logan's Bike Week each year.

items.title: Asked new neighborhoods to connect to the trail system
items.summary: I met with neighborhood councils about new subdivisions such as Willow Lakes. I pressed developers on trail connections, sidewalks and traffic, and asked that a planned trail be built with an earlier phase instead of left for later.

items.title: Made neighborhood block parties easier
items.summary: After a 2026 Utah League of Cities and Towns conference, the Mayor and I launched a simple process for neighbors to close their street for a block party. The city delivers the road-closure signs.

items.title: Supported Logan's Youth City Council
items.summary: I worked with Logan's Youth City Council so high school students get a real seat in local government, including at Local Officials Day at the State Capitol.
